Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls: Dates announced for 12 seats in UP, Uttarakhand, Bengal
Article Text:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, along with a by-election for one seat from West Bengal, on October 16.

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday announced elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal on October 16.The polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and a bypoll to one seat in West Bengal. The notification will be issued on September 29, nominations can be filed until October 6 and counting will take place on October 16, the poll panel said.In Uttar Pradesh, the members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, BL Verma, Seema Dwivedi and Hardeep Singh Puri, Samajwadi Party leader Ram Gopal Yadav and BSP's Ramji Gautam.The seat held by former Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma has been vacant since September 11, when his resignation took effect following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.In Uttarakhand, BJP member Naresh Bansal's term is also ending.Of the 10 outgoing Uttar Pradesh seats, eight are held by BJP, while the Samajwadi Party and BSP hold one each. Based on the current assembly arithmetic, BJP-led alliance is expected to win eight seats, while the Samajwadi Party could secure two.The outcome could leave BSP without representation in the Rajya Sabha as it does not have the numbers to retain Gautam's seat on its own.BSP currently has no MLA in Uttar Pradesh following the death of its lone legislator, Uma Shankar Singh, in August. The party also did not have the numbers to elect a Rajya Sabha member on its own in 2020. However, BJP had fielded only eight candidates for the 10 seats then, allowing BSP's Ramji Gautam to win.BJP is also comfortably placed to retain the Uttarakhand seat.The West Bengal bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of Rukmini Mallik, popularly known as actor Koel Mallick, on July 16. The winner will serve the remainder of the term until April 2, 2032.With a clear majority in the West Bengal Assembly, the ruling BJP is set to wrest the seat from the Trinamool Congress.
Article Summary: Election Commission announces elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats on October 16. Polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and one in West Bengal. Members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar and BL Verma.

Article Title: High number of SIR notices result of rule change after Bihar experience
Article Text:
EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents

NEW DELHI: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission, based on its experience during SIR Phase I in Bihar. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll, over a dozen documents were listed as acceptable proof of birth, citizenship and residence, at the enumeration stage itself.However following the uproar over the inconvenience caused to electors who may not have had these documents and thus faced exclusion, the EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents with the enumeration form (EF) and instead decided to map the electors with the electoral roll from last SIR. The mapping works with inbuilt algorithms to flag logical discrepancies between the last roll and the enumeration forms, based on which notices are automatically issued.“The logical discrepancy detecting software is agnostic and does not distinguish between a VIP and a common man. The fact that election commissioner. S S Sandhu also got a notice due a discrepancy, where his name was mentioned as S S Sandhu in one place and as Sukhbir Singh Sandhu in another, proves this,” an EC functionary pointed out.“The high number of notices seems to unique to urban centres like Delhi, where the electors may have been a little casual while filling up the EF. Also, the BLOs could have been more meticulous in checking forms at the enumeration stage, as this could have cut down the discrepancies that led to the notices,” said an EC official.“If anyone does not return the EF despite three visits of the booth level officer (BLO) to his address and checking by booth level agent (BLA) of political parties, he is either absent, shifted, dead or duplicate elector and his name is not there in draft roll. ⁠If the received EF are incomplete or gives incorrect information, notices are issued.The official added that notices rarely lead to electors’ exclusion and are resolved the moment the elector presents the proof correcting the discrepancy.“No elector is excluded without a hearing, which must be followed by a speaking order, which can, after the final roll be published, be challenged first before the district election officer and then the chief electoral officer,” said an EC official.“Besides, the option of being added back to the electoral roll remains open in perpetuity. Anyone whose name is left out can always fill up Form 6, along with the declaration, on his mobile to get back into the electoral roll,” the official added.
Article Summary: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll. EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents.

Article Title: Many other Shivanis: ‘Tailgated, provoked to race, shown the middle finger’ – a day in the life of women riding bikes
Article Text:
Shivani Chauhan survived a road-rage incident on Gurgaon’s Golf Course Road in which a man in a car chased her and knocked her off her moving bike.

'Danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads': Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick - Pune

‘Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem to digest a woman on two wheels’: Neharika Yadav, Delhi

‘It feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road’ — Soundari Sindy, Chennai

'While going from Gwalior to Hyderabad, a group of men followed me for 45 minutes': Atulya, Rajasthan

Patriarchal conditioning has taught men that women must be watched, judged and corrected — Devika Mehta, Noida

Just treat us like a normal rider — Riya Yadav, Gurgaon

Her injuries will heal, but riding a bike will not be the same again for Shivani Chauhan, who survived a road rage incident in Gurgaon last week in which a man in a car chased Shivani and knocked her off her moving bike on Golf Course Road. “I don't know when I'll start riding again, but whenever I do, I'll have that fear that this can happen again – that another car can come from behind and hit me,” she says.It’s a fear women bike riders understand, and echo, because of what they describe as “unprovoked aggression” that comes their way on roads. Riders TOI spoke to described being chased, tailgated, obstructed, challenged to race and subjected to lewd gestures simply for being women on motorcycles.Delhi-based rider Neharika Yadav said men have chased her from different angles to take photographs or start conversations, while Gurgaon rider Geetika Khurana recalled an incident of men blocking her way and revving alongside her to provoke a race. Male drivers revving their engines, driving dangerously close, honking incessantly – Mumbai-based motorcycle trainer and motivational speaker Shilpa Balakrishnan (51) describes this as a “routine” experience for woman on bikes.“Many have tried to corner me when I overtake. They behave this way simply because they see a woman riding,” she says.The India Women Rider Safety and Mobility Report 2026, based on responses from 542 women riders, found that 57% had experienced harassment on the road.For Shivani (27), who started riding only two years ago, the Sept 13 incident has forever changed the “therapeutic experience” of riding her Aprilia. “The incident keeps playing on my mind on a loop every now and then. It has affected me very badly, I think it will be a long time before I’m able to pick up the bike again,” says Shivani, who had kept her biker identity a secret on social media. As ‘Sia’, she felt freedom.Neharika, a dentist based in Delhi, and Pune-based fashion designer Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick (45) can relate. “I ride a bike because it gives me joy, not because I want to prove anything to anyone. In Delhi-NCR, we get cast into a stereotype. Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem to digest a woman coming on two wheels. Since traffic here is dense, there are men like (Kalyan) Bainsla (who attacked Shivani) who will not give space to a woman rider. They will keep instigating you. I think they get some perverse joy out of it,” she says.Yazarloo-Pattrick says danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads and freedom is the reason they keep paying it. “Such behaviour is an everyday reality. I’m shocked that anyone in India is surprised,” she says. Earlier this month, she was returning from Ladakh when she noticed a black SUV without a number plate following her. She switched on her GoPro but did not try to outrun it. Instead, she slowed down and pulled into a petrol pump. “If someone is chasing me and I cannot safely get away, I always head towards a crowded place.”Soundari Sindy, a lawyer in her mid-30s based out of Chennai, says attitude towards women riding bikes is similar across the country. “It almost feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road,” she tells TOI. A professional racer, Soundari commands a 150cc bike with her 5ft 1in frame. “Snide comments are common. There are strangers who have made fun of me, saying my feet would not touch the ground,” she says.Suparna Sarkar (39), chief instructor at a motorcycle training academy in Gurgaon, tells TOI what made Shivani’s case different was that the aggression was caught on camera. “It’s just that she had a camera, so it led to widespread anger. Girls I teach biking to often share incidents where either people tried to race from behind or they were hit,” she says. Sarkar has experienced it herself. In 2023, she was riding near Mahipalpur in Delhi when a vehicle hit her. “There were no cameras in the area. I didn’t have a camera either,” she says.Sandhya Das, a 38-year-old IT professional who rides with Soundari, agrees that the sight of her on a bike is somehow “not palatable to some men”, whether she is in traditional attire or in biker gear with a jacket and gloves. “Men have tried to zip past me and tried to throw me off balance,” she says.Chetana Naik (37) from Mumbai, who twice encountered a group of make bikers intimidating and overtaking her – in Kashmir recently and in Punjab earlier – adds, “For some men, being overtaken by a woman appears to be an insult that must be avenged. They begin intimidating us till their egos are satisfied,” she says.Professional rider Anita Krishnan says even riding gear can be misread by some motorists as an invitation to race. “They start racing with you. It could be a car or even a bike. They will whizz past you at speed, trying to entice you into a race. This is very common,” she says. For long-distance riders, she points out, jackets, helmets and boots are protection from crashes, flying debris, rain, heat and cold, not racing gear.Krishnan says she sometimes tucks her hair inside her jacket so motorists cannot immediately tell that she is a woman. “The gear also camouflages whether you are a woman. If your hair is out, only then people would know you are a woman. So, I would mostly hide my hair,” she says.For 23-year-old Anainah Batiwala, camouflage goes further. The Mumbaikar does not feel comfortable riding in shorts and, after dark, goes out in baggy clothes. “I dress like a guy in baggy pants,” she says. “I wear my actual going-out clothes underneath.”Atulya (23) remembers being scared for her life a couple of years ago while travelling from Gwalior to Hyderabad. A group of men followed her bike relentlessly for about 45 minutes on the highway. “I kept riding for about 10-15km even after I lost them. I was so scared that something would happen to me if I applied the brakes,” she says.Atulya (23) remembers being scared for her life a couple of years ago while travelling from Gwalior to Hyderabad. A group of men followed her bike relentlessly for about 45 minutes on the highway. “I kept riding for about 10-15km even after I lost them. I was so scared that something would happen to me if I applied the brakes,” she says.Atulya, who is originally from Kerala but grew up in Rajasthan, has been riding her bike all over India from the age of 18. While the incident rattled her, she decided to keep going.Delhi-based biker Meenakshi says long group rides can become particularly vulnerable on the return journey because riders who set out together often disperse while heading home. “Often, we get calls from riders asking for help from passers-by, or they call us to say that two or three people are following them,” she says. Krishnan says women travelling alone or in smaller groups also become more selective about where they stop after dark and often share their live location with family members.Organised riding groups have built formal safety systems around that vulnerability. Some assign a leader at the front, a tail rider to make sure nobody is left behind, and a marshal to keep both ends connected. “Men may have the liberty to stop anywhere, but women have to take extra precaution,” says Saify Ratlamwala, who runs riding groups in Navi Mumbai.Devika Mehta, a media professional from Noida, narrates how a BMW came dangerously close to her bike on a curved road, nearly running her off.“Remarks, lewd gestures, honking, and constant stares make our freedom rides really ugly. If they don’t hit you, they will come extremely close or follow to just mess with you,” the 40-year-old says, blaming this behaviour on “generations of patriarchal conditioning that has taught men that women must be watched, judged and corrected”. “Add weak impulse control, peer bravado, lax policing and near-zero consequences and harassment starts to feel normal, even entertaining, to them,” Devika says.Geetika (25), a PR professional based in Gurgaon, said catcalling, teasing and obstructing the way are things most women riders have gone through in NCR. “The day I took my first ride, the experience was not pleasant. A group of boys obstructed my way and challenged me to race with them by coming close and revving their bikes. Since then, I’ve only taken my bike out early morning when I’m assured of encountering the least traffic. ”Sarkar says it’s “not all bad that women just can’t ride on Delhi-NCR roads”, but agreed there is a “section of people who create nuisance” and that can happen anytime. “It’s not only a women rider problem, but a women safety and road safety issue. When people are on the road, they should behave. When someone is driving a car, there is a base, there is support, it will not lose balance. But when you are on a two-wheeler, even the minutest touch will make you fall,” adds Sarkar.Though less exposed than those on two-wheelers, women who drive cars say they have also encountered a “sense of entitlement” from strangers on the road, including cab drivers.Pooja (38), who has been driving for 12 years in Delhi, says comments are common, not because she has done anything to provoke it but because it’s a woman at the wheel. “I keep getting told by strangers that the size of my car (a Scorpio) doesn’t ‘match’ mine.”Rupali, an advertising professional from Noida, says she once deliberately slowed down to let a group of men overtake her in their car, just so she wouldn’t be harassed. This did not deter them. “They stopped and waited for me to pass, rolled down the windows and showed me their middle fingers,” the 35-year-old says. After they sped off, Rupali says, she drove at 30kmph so she wouldn’t encounter them again.Yet the hostility has not stopped more women from taking up motorcycles. Meenakshi says the number of women she sees learning to ride has increased sharply. “Three years ago, if I trained 10 women in a month, the number would be 60-70 now,” she says. The profile, according to Krishnan, is changing too, with women in their 40s, 50s and even 60s increasingly taking up long-distance riding.Dnyanadaa Mhaskar is an example of that change. The Navi Mumbai schoolteacher began riding at 41, bought a motorcycle while still on a learner’s licence and, by her own account, barely knew how to work the clutch and gears. She later borrowed her grocer’s 100cc Hero for a ride to Pune and joined an all-women motorcycling group. Now 54, she says simply: “Riding is my solace and my bike is my soulmate.”Riya Yadav, a Gurgaon-based professional biker who has been riding since she was a teenager, adds, “People need to realise that we are just riding a bike. We are not doing some rocket science. Just treat us like a normal rider.”Most of these women say they have learnt to live with the unwanted attention on roads. “I think society at large has to change for us to see any meaningful change in men’s mindset towards a female driver. Till then, women need to take utmost precautions while riding. And be brave,” Shivani says.
Article Summary: India Women Rider Safety and Mobility Report 2026, based on responses from 542 women riders, found that 57% had experienced harassment on the road. Riders TOI spoke to described being chased, tailgated, obstructed, challenged to race and subjected to lewd gestures simply for being women on motorcycles.

Article Title: Lt Gen Mohit Seth to be new GOC of White Knight Corps
Article Text:
Maj Gen Mohit Seth took over as the General Officer Commanding (GOC) relieving Maj Gen SS Slaria who has moved to Headquarter Northern Command.

JAMMU: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth will take over as the new General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s Nagrota-based White Knight Corps (16 Corps) on Oct 1. He will replace Lt Gen P K Mishra, who will move to a new posting, officials said.In his distinguished military career spanning over three decades, Lt Gen Seth has served in key command and staff positions in J&K, the northeast, and at the Army HQ. He is currently the Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team in Bhutan.Lt Gen Seth previously was GOC of the Counter-Insurgency Force Kilo (Kilo Force), an elite formation of the Army’s Rashtriya Rifles tasked with anti-terror operations in north Kashmir. He has also served as the Indian Army Liaison Officer at the High Commission of India, United Kingdom.
Article Summary: Lt Gen Mohit Seth will take over as the new General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s Nagrota-based White Knight Corps (16 Corps) He will replace Lt Gen P K Mishra, who will move to a new posting, officials said.

Article Title: The 'chosen one' for a role in BSP is Ishan: Mayawati's latest U-turn in ongoing family drama
Article Text:
Mayawati’s chosen one is Ishan Anand.

A warning for Ishan

Niece loses the race

Doors forever closed for Akash Anand?

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

The Kanshi Ram reference

The Ambedkar example

Road ahead for Ishan

NEW DELHI: Mayawati’s chosen one is Ishan Anand. Or is he? Well, at least for now. There’s another twist in the ongoing succession drama in the BSP chief’s family. Younger nephew Ishan, who was ruled out from getting any position in the BSP only ten days back, has ended up winning Mayawati’s “trust test” for a role in the party.“Only Shri Ishan Anand from Shri Anand Kumar’s family will now be promoted by giving him a respectable responsibility in the party,” Mayawati announced on X on Sunday.So, when the BSP holds its national-level meeting in Lucknow on September 23, Ishan is likely to get a “respectable responsibility” in the party. This will be 20 days after his elder brother Akash Anand was shown the door at a similar meeting held on September 3. Ishan, Akash and their sister Deepika are children of Mayawati’s younger brother Anand Kumar, who has been “working in Mayawati’s service for many years.”But Ishan’s promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to “rise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication.”There was a clear and strong warning for Ishan. “If he commits any serious act against the party, he too will be shown the door from the party.But in such a situation, no other member of Shri Anand Kumar’s family will be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party,” Mayawati announced.In a long post on X on September 12, the BSP chief had ruled out any political role for her nephews Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, but left room for Deepika to take on responsibilities in the party if the need arises.The BSP chief had said, "Today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP. If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand, who is currently studying law. He can then, based on her honesty, loyalty, and efficiency, assign her his own responsibilities within the party as needed. "But that did not happen.In her post, Mayawati dwelled on the “dilemma” she faced in making the decision and also shared the yardstick she used to decide the “chosen one.”“The question of who from Shri Anand Kumar’s family I should or should not promote in the party has been a matter of considerable dilemma for me for some time. Bringing this dilemma to an end, and after giving serious thought to every aspect, I have now decided that if any member of his family is to be promoted in the party, it should be someone who does not follow Akash’s footsteps in any way.”“As for seeking help from his daughter in the future, after she gets married, if her case also turns out to be like Shri Akash Anand’s, that too would not be in the interest of the party. Keeping such a possibility in mind, it would now be appropriate in the interest of the party to completely keep Shri Akash Anand and his sister away from being given any responsibility in the party. In other words, there will be no change whatsoever in this decision,” Mayawati wrote in her post.Akash Anand, who was groomed for years and, at least on two occasions in the past, announced as Mayawati’s “political successor,” now seems completely out of the picture. At least for now.“On special request of Shri Anand Kumar, I had to promote his elder son, Shri Akash Anand, in politics. Since his marriage, however, Shri Akash Anand’s conduct and activities at every step have been such that, a few days ago, I once again had to separate him from the party,” Mayawati said in her latest post.“In other words, he is now completely caught up in the web of his father-in-law, Shri Ashok Siddharth. Bringing him back into the party now would amount to a major betrayal of the party, and I can never commit such an act against the party,” she wrote.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSP’s national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.However, now with his younger brother taking the centre stage, it may not be easy for Akash to claw back into the power structure.The BSP chief shared her mantra for success in politics. “I want to tell the people of the party that, keeping my own experience in mind, if they want to succeed in politics and do something for society, they must, like me, rise above their attachment to their brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication,” Mayawati wrote in the post.She then referred to the role of BSP founder Kanshi Ram in showing her the path“The founder and architect of the BSP, respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji, after entering politics, always kept himself away from giving political benefits to his close relatives and family members. He allowed them to work in the party organisation only with a selfless spirit. Not only this, he devoted his entire life to the interests and welfare of the ‘Bahujan Samaj’, without creating a family of his own,” Maywati wrote.“Inspired by him, I too decided to follow in his footsteps and devoted my entire life to the ‘Bahujan Samaj’. However, because I am a woman, I was compelled to always keep one of my brothers or sisters with me. Under this arrangement, my younger brother, Shri Anand Kumar, has been working in my service for many years,” the BSP chief said.Justifying her move, Mayawati wrote, “I have taken this decision in the interest of the party and the movement, inspired by respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji and influenced by a letter written by the revered Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar.”The BSP chief stated that Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar had written a letter on February 23, 1956, warning his son Yashwant B Ambedkar over his alleged attempts to try and take control of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press.To convey her message to Ishan and others, Mayawati cited the strong stand taken by Ambedkar against his son, “I have to inform you that I have received several communications from Shri Upsham saying that you are not allowing him to perform his duties as the accountant and cashier of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press. You seem to think that by doing this you will take control of the press. I am warning you that the press is public property; it belongs neither to you nor to me, and it is not possible to permit any kind of irregularity in a public account.Your conduct has not been proper... If you do not heed my final and last instructions, I will remove you from the press and, if you do not heed this warning, I will also prosecute you.”‘Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown’: Well, that’s perhaps how one can describe Ishan’s future in BSP. We will have to wait and see what respectable role he gets from Mayawati on September 23 when the party meets. However, irrespective of the role, the road ahead for Ishan would be challenging.
Article Summary: BSP chief Mayawati's chosen one is Ishan Anand, at least for now. Ishan's promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to “rise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication”

Article Title: Owaisi opens alliance door in UP; Congress warns AIMIM could end up helping BJP
Article Text:
Imran Masood said only Congress can take BJP on. (ANI)

Owaisi's alliance pitch

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Akhilesh sets 27,000-vote target

NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh gearing up for the 2027 assembly elections, Congress MP Imran Masood on Monday took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi 's alliance pitch, warning that the party's presence in the polls "would end up benefitting BJP."His remarks came a day after Owaisi said AIMIM was open to an alliance with "like-minded" parties seeking to prevent the BJP from returning to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term.Speaking to ANI, Masood said, "If an alliance is to be formed, it should be finalised; otherwise, we must proceed with our own preparations. The political climate, not just here, but across the entire country, is such that one cannot move forward without the Congress; the Congress is essential. A fight against the BJP can only be waged with the Congress; only the Congress can take them on.""Rahul Gandhi's leadership is capable of overcoming them. Finalise it (alliance) immediately. I am not aware of who is in touch; I have no information regarding that so far. If it isn't finalised, the damage happens on the ground," he added.Responding to Owaisi's proposal, Masood said defeating the BJP was the primary objective but argued that strategic voting would be important."Defeating the BJP is the primary objective, and Muslims alone cannot defeat the BJP. If the BJP wins and forms the government, it is the Muslims who suffer the consequences. The political atmosphere in Hyderabad is different from that in Uttar Pradesh. Owaisi Ji might win 4-5 seats, but he ends up facilitating a BJP government. What will you do with those five MLAs? If a BJP government is formed, who suffers the loss? Since the BJP would form the government, people need to act sensibly. People must make decisions wisely and astutely," he said.Owaisi had earlier on Sunday said that AIMIM was ready to work with parties that share its objective of keeping the BJP out of power in Uttar Pradesh."We do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone," Owaisi said.Owaisi also cited AIMIM's experience in Bihar, saying the party had sought an alliance with opposition parties and asked for six seats, but the proposal was not accepted. He said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh irrespective of alliance talks.Earlier in the day, Owaisi, meanwhile, said AIMIM was already preparing for the Uttar Pradesh elections and was hopeful of sending its candidates to the state Assembly."We are visiting specifically in connection with election preparations. Our party is fully prepared and actively gearing up; we are hopeful that this time our candidates will be elected as MLAs and enter the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly," he said.On the possibility of an alliance, Owaisi said, "Wait until October 2nd; we will let you know by then."The Congress's push for an early alliance decision also comes as the Samajwadi Party steps up its preparations for the 2027 polls. At the party's state executive meeting on Sunday, Akhilesh Yadav said the SP would work to increase its vote share by 27,000 votes in every assembly constituency."Today was our state executive meeting. In this, we have decided that in the 2027 assembly elections, we will work to increase 27,000 votes in every assembly seat. That means we will reduce 27,000 votes of the BJP," Yadav said.Masood also criticised the Election Commission over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) notices, questioning the difficulties they could create for ordinary citizens."What could be more farcical in this country than a situation where Members of Parliament, former Chief Ministers, and even the External Affairs Minister receive such notices? If they are getting notices, the Election Commission's situation couldn't be more absurd. Imagine the plight of the common man or those who are unemployed and struggling just to find a single meal a day. Are they expected to run around with documents? Look at the state the country has been reduced to, constantly standing in queues. The system has failed. The system has completely collapsed," he said.

Article Title: 31 years ago, Ganesha ‘drank’ milk and India went viral: How a September 21, 1995 claim spread from temple to temple, crossed borders within hours and became a global story without social media
Article Text:

What made the episode so unusual

The first great pre-social-media viral phenomenon?

And somehow, by the end of that extraordinary day, a spoonful of milk had become a global story.

Thirty-one years ago, on September 21, 1995, I came home from school to find that something was strangely different. My aunt, who would diligently wait for me every day and was always the one to serve me lunch, was missing. She was more than just the person who fed me; she would sit with me, tell me interesting stories and make the afternoon feel special.I looked for her everywhere. Finally, the housemaid arrived with my plate of dal and rice and casually told me, “Didi has gone to feed milk to Lord Ganesha.”I was puzzled. What did she mean? After lunch, I called a friend from the landline. She had the same story. Her mother, too, was not at home. By evening, my aunt returned, visibly excited, and told my mother, who had just come back from work, what she had seen.“I took a spoon of milk to feed Ganesha, and the milk disappeared,” she said. My mother looked at her in disbelief. “Really?” she asked. “Really. I saw it with my own eyes,” she insisted, quite overwhelmed with emotions.The news spread fast, Ganesha idols were apparently drinking milk. There were no smartphones, social media platforms, WhatsApp groups or instant notifications to amplify the news.India’s internet had only just arrived, television was still dominated by Doordarshan, and newspapers remained the primary source of next-day news. Yet, within hours, temples were overflowing, milk was disappearing from shops and the story had travelled beyond India.It was not the age of viral news. In fact viral was the world synonymous with just one thing-the infectious disease of influenza. There was no way to immediately search the internet, watch a viral video or check social media posts from another city. Then what caused the spread of this frenzy? According to a contemporary Times of India report Mumbai and several other parts of India were swept by reports that Ganesha idols were accepting milk offerings. The report described the news as spreading “like wildfire” as thousands of devotees rushed to temples.The crucial point was that people did not merely hear the claim. They went to temples and tried it for themselves. Devotees carried spoons filled with milk towards the trunks or mouths of Ganesha idols, and many reported seeing the milk disappear.The episode becomes even more extraordinary when viewed against India's technological landscape in 1995. Public internet access had only just been launched by VSNL in August that year. According to historicalinternet use in India in 1995 stood at just 0.026% of the population.Telephones were also far from universal. India had approximately 11.98 million fixed telephone connections in 1995, equivalent to around 1.24 fixed lines per 100 people.This meant that the mechanisms of mass communication were fundamentally different from those available today. A person could call a relative, but there was no instant group messaging system through which hundreds of people could receive the same information simultaneously. News moved through conversations, local networks, religious communities, radio, television and newspapers. And yet the Ganesha story moved extraordinarily quickly.It would be inaccurate to suggest that India had only Doordarshan in 1995. The country's television landscape had already begun changing. Zee TV had launched in 1992, Star TV had entered the Indian market in 1991 and Sony Entertainment Television launched in 1995. But the explosion of private, round-the-clock news channels that would later transform India's news culture was still years away.Doordarshan nevertheless remained hugely influential . An academic study citing Ministry of Information & Broadcasting figures puts India's television universe in 1995 at approximately 40 million television households and 250 million viewers.There was therefore a very different relationship between an event and the news cycle. Newspapers generally reported what had happened the previous day, television had scheduled programming rather than today's constant breaking-news stream, and there was no digital ecosystem continuously refreshing itself. The Ganesha phenomenon had to travel through people before it could become a mass media story.The reports quickly produced visible consequences. A contemporary Los Angeles Times repor published on September 23, 1995, said millions of Indians had rushed to test the phenomenon and reported that milk had “virtually disappeared” from shops in New Delhi by noon.That detail captures the extraordinary feedback loop created by the phenomenon. People heard that Ganesha was drinking milk, went out to buy milk, took it to temples and offered it to idols. The resulting rush itself became evidence of how seriously the story was being taken.Contemporary reports described crowds gathering at temples, with devotees carrying spoons, bowls and containers of milk.The most remarkable part of the episode was perhaps how quickly it crossed India's borders. Reports soon emerged from Hindu communities in Britain, the United States, Canada, Nepal and elsewhere. A contemporary os Angeles Times report noted that the reports had spread beyond India to Hindu communities in other countries, including Britain and Los Angeles. Hinduism Today later recalled receiving telephone calls and fax messages from different parts of the world reporting similar experiences. Its contemporary account provides a fascinating glimpse into how an international religious community communicated before email, social media and messaging apps became commonplace.The technology may appear primitive by today's standards, but the human network was remarkably effective. Someone in India could telephone a relative abroad, that person could contact a local temple, and within hours another community could be trying the same experiment.The story did not need an algorithm to travel. It travelled through relationships.As the reports spread, scientists and sceptics began examining what devotees were observing. One of the principal scientific explanations involved capillary action and surface tension. Rather than the idol literally consuming the milk, the liquid could move along the surface of the material, creating the appearance that it was being absorbed by the idol.For devotees, however, the scientific explanation did not necessarily invalidate what they had experienced. The same physical observation could be interpreted through very different frameworks: as a religious sign by believers, as a scientific phenomenon by researchers, and as an extraordinary mass social event by journalists.Looking back from the age of smartphones, the 1995 episode is remarkable not simply because of what people believed they were seeing, but because of how quickly the information travelled.India's public internet had only just begun. Fixed telephone connections were limited, television was expanding but had not yet become the 24-hour news environment of today, and newspapers operated on a fundamentally different news cycle. Yet within hours, a local report had become a national phenomenon and then an international story.A telephone call led to another telephone call. A conversation at one temple led to another. Newspapers carried the story forward, television added another layer of coverage and international media transformed what had begun as a local religious phenomenon into a global news story.Calling the Ganesha milk episode the world's first viral phenomenon would be too absolute. Stories travelled internationally long before 1995, through newspapers, radio, television and word of mouth.But the episode offers a remarkable case study of mass communication before the social-media era. Millions of people participated in the same rapidly spreading story without having access to the tools that today make such mass participation almost instantaneous.That is what makes September 21, 1995, worth remembering 31 years later. The question is no longer simply whether Ganesha idols were actually drinking milk. The episode has another story to tell, about technology, faith, communication and human networks.In 2026, information can travel around the world in seconds. In 1995, it travelled from person to person, from telephone to telephone, from temple to temple and eventually from newspaper to newspaper.(All images are AI Generated)
Article Summary: A spoonful of milk had become a global story in September 1995. India's internet had only just arrived, television was still dominated by Doordarshan. There was no way to immediately search the internet, watch a viral video or check social media posts from another city.

Article Title: In 2014, Naomi Osaka’s family faced eviction while she was still chasing her tennis breakthrough; a year later, she had earned just $6,290 in six months before becoming a four-time Grand Slam champion
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka’s family faced eviction while she was still chasing her tennis breakthrough(Getty Images)

The family gamble behind the Stanford breakthrough

The Grand Slam years changed the scale

From endorsements to investments and ownership

A new chapter in 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Naomi Osaka was 16 when her family received an eviction notice on their Florida condominium. Her professional tennis career was still developing, and her earnings were nowhere near enough to provide financial security. A year later, she had earned just $6,290 during the first six months of 2015, a figure that looks very different against the career she would eventually build.More than a decade later, Osaka has four Grand Slam singles titles, a former world No. 1 ranking and a career that stretches beyond tennis into investments, sports ownership, media and fashion.Osaka’s professional journey began with her father, Leonard François, who coached Naomi and her older sister Mari. François was inspired by Richard Williams and chose to develop his daughters outside the traditional American junior tennis system. The family had moved from Japan to the United States when Naomi was three and eventually settled in Florida.The financial pressure became particularly difficult in 2014. According to details from Ben Rothenberg’s biography of Osaka reported by Tennis.com, the family received an eviction notice on their Pembroke Pines condominium about a month before Naomi entered qualifying at the Bank of the West Classic in Stanford.They were given six weeks to leave, at a time when the sisters’ tennis careers had not produced enough income to cover the family’s expenses.The Stanford tournament soon gave Osaka an opportunity to change that picture. The 16-year-old qualified for the main draw and faced Samantha Stosur, the 2011 US Open champion and a former world No. 4. Osaka defeated Stosur in three sets, earning $10,000 in prize money and attracting greater attention from sponsors.Her finances were still modest after the breakthrough. According to the same biography details, Osaka earned only $6,290 during the first six months of 2015, while Mari earned $2,160 during the same period. Osaka was still climbing the professional rankings, with the Grand Slam titles and commercial success that would eventually transform her career still ahead of her.Osaka’s rise accelerated in 2018 when she won her first WTA title at Indian Wells. Later that year, she reached the US Open final and defeated Serena Williams 6-2, 6-4 to claim her first Grand Slam singles championship.The following January brought another major breakthrough. Osaka defeated Petra Kvitova in the 2019 Australian Open final to win her second consecutive Grand Slam title and became the first Japanese player to reach No. 1 in the WTA rankings. She was 21 years and 104 days old when she reached the top position.Naomi Osaka added another US Open title in 2020 and another Australian Open championship in 2021, taking her Grand Slam total to four. Her success also transformed her commercial profile. Forbes estimated that she earned $37.4 million between June 2019 and June 2020, including $34 million from endorsements and $3.4 million in prize money, making her the highest-paid female athlete on its list for that period.That was a dramatic change from the $6,290 she had earned during the first half of 2015. Osaka had gone from a teenager trying to establish herself on the professional circuit to an athlete whose name carried major commercial value, and she began using that platform to pursue opportunities beyond sponsorships.Osaka’s business career began taking a different shape as she started investing in companies and taking ownership positions. In 2019, she invested in BodyArmor and received an equity stake in the sports drink company. Coca-Cola acquired the remaining 85% of BodyArmor in 2021 in a deal that valued the company at $5.6 billion.She also moved into sports ownership. In 2021, Osaka became an investor in the North Carolina Courage of the National Women’s Soccer League. When the club announced the investment, she spoke about the women who had supported her while she was growing up and connected her decision to opportunities for women in sport.“The women who have invested in me growing up made me who I am today,” Osaka said in the club’s announcement. She also said she wanted to invest in women who could become role models and leaders.Her own ventures added another dimension. Osaka launched KINLÒ in 2021, a skincare and suncare brand developed with melanated skin in mind. In 2022, she and Stuart Duguid launched Hana Kuma, a media company focused on stories and creators from different backgrounds. The company later raised $5 million as it expanded its work across entertainment and culture.Osaka has also invested in other consumer businesses. In 2024, she participated in funding rounds involving companies including Pressed Roots and W, adding more ventures to a portfolio that has continued to grow alongside her tennis career.Osaka’s business interests have continued to expand in 2026, with fashion becoming one of her newest areas of focus. In August, she unveiled a prototype for a luxury leather-goods project with designer Mike Cherman at Uncharted’s Fame to Fortune Summit. Osaka described the project as her “biggest dream” outside tennis while explaining how her success in the sport had created opportunities to invest and work with people who could help develop her ideas.Her professional setup also changed at the beginning of the year. Osaka left Evolve, the sports agency she had co-founded with Duguid, at the end of 2025 and returned to IMG for tennis representation in January 2026.On the court, Osaka remains an active professional in 2026, with the WTA listing four Grand Slam titles and a career-high No. 1 ranking. Her return to major competition has added another chapter to a career that has included a rapid rise, a period away from the tour and a return to professional tennis after becoming a mother.The contrast with her early years is difficult to miss. In 2014, her family was dealing with an eviction notice while Osaka was still searching for her first major breakthrough. In the first six months of 2015, she had earned $6,290. Within a few years, her annual earnings were being measured in tens of millions of dollars, while her career expanded into investments, ownership and businesses of her own.In 2026, Osaka is still competing as a Grand Slam champion, but tennis is now only one part of her professional life. Her investments, sports ownership, media work and luxury fashion project show how the platform created by her tennis career has developed into a much broader business career.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka was 16 when her family received an eviction notice on their Florida condominium. Her professional tennis career was still developing, and her earnings were nowhere near enough to provide financial security. A year later, she had earned just $6,290 during the first six months of 2015.

NEW DELHI: Shafali Verma continued her sensational run in T20I cricket in 2026, rewriting another record during India's Asian Games gold-medal clash against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.The India opener became the highest run-scorer in a calendar year in women's T20Is, surpassing South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt . Shafali's 29-ball 48 in the gold-medal match took her tally for the year to 863 runs, moving past Wolvaardt's 824.Shafali's innings at Korogi Sports Park featured three fours and three sixes and came at a strike rate of 165.52. Although she fell short of another half-century, her latest contribution extended a remarkable run in the shortest format.In 24 T20Is in 2026, Shafali has now scored 863 runs at an average of 39.22 and a strike rate of 162.83. Her tally includes one century and seven fifties, with a best score of 100 not out.Wolvaardt, meanwhile, has scored 824 runs in 24 matches this year at an average of 43.36 and a strike rate of 138.72. Her tally includes two centuries and four fifties, with a best of 126 not out.Shafali's record-breaking year has been driven by an extraordinary sequence of performances in knockout matches since the 2025 Women's World Cup final.After scoring 87 against South Africa in the World Cup final, she has maintained her aggressive approach across the Asia Cup and Asian Games. Her scores in her last five T20Is read 64, 68, 40 not out, 100 not out and 48.She scored 64 off 40 balls against Bangladesh in the Asia Cup semifinal before following it with 68 off 39 in the final against Sri Lanka.At the Asian Games, Shafali smashed 40 not out from just 15 balls against Japan in the quarterfinal before producing a spectacular unbeaten 100 off 49 balls against Bangladesh in the semifinal.Her 48 against Sri Lanka in the final completed an extraordinary stretch of six innings in which she has amassed 407 runs at an average of 101.75, including one century and three fifties.Shafali's latest milestone came on the same day she and Smriti Mandhana extended their record as the most prolific partnership in women's T20I cricket.The pair's opening stand of 99 against Sri Lanka took their aggregate partnership tally beyond 4,000 runs. Mandhana and Shafali have now combined for 4,080 runs in 107 matches at an average of 39.23, including six century partnerships and 26 fifty-plus stands.The UAE pair of Esha Oza and Theertha Satish are second on the list with 2,949 partnership runs, followed by Australia's Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney with 2,720.
Article Summary: Shafali Verma becomes highest run-scorer in a calendar year in women's T20Is. India opener surpasses South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt. Shafali's 29-ball 48 in the gold-medal match took her tally for the year to 863 runs.

Article Title: Michael Jordan retired 23 years ago, Tiger Woods barely plays, yet they still out-earn even Ronaldo and remain the highest-earning athletes in sports history
Article Text:
Michael Jordan (left). Image via: James Gilbert/ Getty Images, Tiger woods (Right). Image via: Instagram

How Jordan and Woods stayed ahead without having to compete

A Fortune That No Longer Depends on the Scoreboard

The Deal Nike Almost Walked Away From

What the Trophies Actually Bought Them

A List Built on What Happens After the Applause Stops

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael Jordan has been away from professional basketball since 2003, while Tiger Woods has spent years appearing only intermittently in competitive golf and has not officially retired. Neither is producing the kind of sporting income associated with the world's biggest active stars, yet both remain above them on the all-time earnings list.Michael Jordan has not stepped onto an NBA court in twenty-three years, and Tiger Woods has spent the better part of the last decade managing injuries rather than chasing majors, and yet neither man has been overtaken at the top of sport's all-time earnings ledger. According to Sportico's latest ranking of career earnings through the end of 2025, adjusted for inflation, Jordan sits first with $4.5 billion, Woods follows at $2.88 billion, and only then does the list arrive at Cristiano Ronaldo, the highest-paid athlete still competing, at $2.52 billion. LeBron James and Lionel Messi round out the top five, both of them still playing at the highest level, both of them still a considerable distance behind two men whose competitive careers effectively ended long ago.What makes this year's numbers worth pausing over is not simply that Jordan remains on top, since he has occupied that position for years, but that the gap separating him from Woods grew rather than shrank, expanding from roughly $850 million a year earlier to about $1.31 billion now, a jump of some $460 million in the space of twelve months. Two athletes who no longer need to compete are, in some sense, still winning.There was a period, decades ago now, when Jordan and Woods earned their fortunes the conventional way, by being unmistakably the best at what they did and letting the money follow the performance. Jordan built his early reputation on championships with the Chicago Bulls, and Woods built his on a run of major titles that reshaped what golf could commercially become, and in both cases the athlete and the business around him grew together during those years.Their playing careers have since slowed dramatically, Jordan's ending outright in 2003 and Woods's fading into sporadic, injury-interrupted appearances rather than a formal retirement, and yet the businesses attached to their names kept expanding well past the point where either man could carry them through performance alone.Jordan's estimated earnings for 2025 alone came to $275 million, a figure that quietly exceeded what Ronaldo made over the same period despite Ronaldo still playing at an elite level for Al-Nassr, and it also came to roughly twice the $137 million earned by Canelo Alvarez, who ranked second among active athletes for the year. None of that money arrived through a late-career contract or a surprise return to competitive basketball. It arrived through a business relationship that Jordan signed into as a twenty-one-year-old rookie, one that has since grown so large that its continued output no longer has anything to do with whether Jordan ever plays basketball again.Nike's original agreement with Jordan, signed in 1984 before he had appeared in a single professional game, was worth $2.5 million over five years and included a base salary of $500,000 annually, roughly three times what other NBA players were getting from shoe companies at the time.Buried inside that contract was a clause allowing Nike to exit the deal entirely if Jordan's shoes failed to generate $4 million in sales, a provision that reveals how uncertain the whole arrangement looked at the outset. Nike was, by most measures, an odd choice for a rising basketball star to align himself with, given that Adidas was generating about fifty per cent more revenue at the time, Reebok was closing in fast enough to overtake Nike by 1987, and Converse already had the league's biggest names, including Magic Johnson, Larry Bird and Julius Erving, wearing its shoes.What separated Jordan's contract from those of his contemporaries was a cut of sales built into the terms, meaning that as the shoes sold, his earnings grew alongside them rather than stopping at a fixed salary. Those shoes went on to generate more than $100 million in their first year alone, and the business built on that foundation has continued compounding for four decades, with the Jordan Brand pulling in $7.3 billion in revenue for the fiscal year ending May 2025, even after a sixteen per cent decline during a turnaround led by Nike's chief executive Elliott Hill.Woods, working in a different sport but along a strikingly similar path, spent twenty-seven years under a Nike deal of his own before the partnership ended in 2024, since which time he has built out sponsorships with Rolex, TaylorMade and Monster Energy, alongside ventures spanning golf technology, entertainment, course design and real estate through companies like TMRW Sports, PopStroke and Full Swing, the last of which was acquired by Versant Media Group for approximately $530 million in a deal completed this past August.Woods's competitive record, set against his financial one, tells an unusual story about where professional golf's money actually sits. He has won 82 PGA Tour events and 15 major championships across his career, yet his tournament prize money adds up to only about $121 million, a modest figure next to the nearly $2 billion Forbes estimates he has earned pretax since turning professional.His last major victory came at the 2019 Masters, an improbable comeback at forty-three years old after an eleven-year gap between titles, and his most recent completed PGA Tour event was the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut entirely. He did appear at the TGL Finals in March 2026, representing Jupiter Links GC, only to be involved in a rollover car accident three days later that forced him away from the game once again while he recovers from an Achilles tendon rupture sustained the previous year and a seventh back surgery completed in October 2025.Jordan's situation involves no comparable physical setback, simply the passage of twenty-three years since he last competed professionally, and yet Q Scores data cited by Sportico found his public awareness rating still sits at 78 per cent, the highest of any athlete surveyed, with Woods following at 70 per cent alongside Serena Williams, and Shaquille O'Neal and Tom Brady trailing slightly behind at 75 and 73 per cent respectively. Jordan's likability score came in at 28, the highest recorded among the athletes surveyed, while Woods scored 11, actually below the average for sports personalities generally, a gap that suggests the two men's continued earning power rests on different foundations even as their financial outcomes look remarkably similar.Looking across the full ranking rather than just its top two names, the broader pattern becomes harder to ignore. David Beckham, Roger Federer and Tom Brady each earned more than $50 million in 2025 through commercial arrangements alone, despite none of them currently competing in their sports, and the top 50 athletes collectively have generated approximately $56.2 billion in inflation-adjusted earnings through the end of 2025, spanning ten different sports, with basketball contributing the most names at 13, followed by golf with eight and boxing with seven.Only 18 of the 50 athletes on the list remain actively competing, and 20 have crossed the billion-dollar threshold in career earnings, with the cutoff for inclusion sitting around $595 million, a mark currently held by the retired Formula 1 driver Kimi Räikkönen.Serena Williams remains the only woman to appear anywhere on the list, with approximately $680 million in career earnings, and perhaps most tellingly, not a single athlete under the age of 30 has made the cut at all, a gap that seems likely to close given how dramatically on-field salaries and endorsement markets have grown for the current generation.Ronaldo, James and Messi continue adding to their totals every year they keep playing, chasing performance bonuses and new contracts the way athletes always have, while Jordan and Woods sit above them having already crossed into a different category entirely, one where the money keeps arriving regardless of whether either man ever plays again. Jordan stopped being merely a basketball player a long time ago, and it is that transformation, more than anything he ever did on a court, that keeps his name at the very top of a list built to measure exactly this kind of staying power.
Article Summary: Michael Jordan has been away from professional basketball since 2003. Tiger Woods has spent years appearing only intermittently in competitive golf and has not officially retired. Neither is producing the kind of sporting income associated with the world's biggest active stars. Yet both remain above them on the all-time earnings list.

Article Title: Smriti Mandhana scripts history, becomes first woman to score 11,000 international runs
Article Text:
Smriti Mandhana (Pic credit: BCCI Women)

From Mithali Raj's record to 11,000-run landmark

Mandhana, Shafali extend record partnership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana added another landmark to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, becoming the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs in international cricket during India's Asian Games gold-medal final against Sri Lanka at Korogi Sports Park in Aichi-Nagoya.Mandhana entered the final needing just 13 runs to reach the landmark. She had accumulated 10,987 runs across Tests, ODIs and T20Is, with 788 in Tests, 5,411 in ODIs and 4,788 in T20Is. She wasted little time getting to the historic mark after India opted to bat first.The India vice-captain began with two boundaries in the opening over before launching a six in the third over to complete 11,000 international runs. The milestone added another chapter to a remarkable run of record-breaking performances for the left-hander.Mandhana had only recently taken the record for the most runs in women's international cricket across formats from former India captain Mithali Raj . She overtook Raj's tally of 10,868 runs with a spectacular 124 against Hong Kong in the Women's Asia Cup earlier this month, taking her total to 10,880 at the time.The 30-year-old has continued to rewrite the record books in the shortest format as well. During India's Asian Games semifinal against Bangladesh, Mandhana surpassed New Zealand great Suzie Bates to become the leading run-scorer in women's T20Is.She achieved the T20I milestone during her 37 off 19 balls in India's 114-run win over Bangladesh. At that point, Mandhana moved to 4,788 T20I runs, ahead of Bates' 4,758.Her latest landmark in the Asian Games final came just two weeks after she had established herself as the leading run-scorer in women's international cricket. Her 124 against Hong Kong was also her 18th international century, taking her past Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt for the most hundreds in women's international cricket at the time.Mandhana's rapid accumulation of milestones has made the Asian Games a particularly memorable tournament for her. She also became the first Indian woman to hit 100 sixes in T20Is during the semifinal against Bangladesh.Mandhana also reached her half-century in the gold-medal clash off just 31 balls, continuing her aggressive start alongside Shafali Verma.The pair's latest stand further extended their record as the most prolific partnership in women's T20I cricket. Their aggregate partnership runs moved beyond 4,000, comfortably ahead of the UAE's Esha Oza and Theertha Satish, who are second on the list with 2,949 runs.Their partnership in the final also crossed another significant mark, with Mandhana and Shafali adding 99 runs against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.India entered the final unchanged after beating Japan by eight wickets in the quarterfinal and Bangladesh by 114 runs in the semifinal. Sri Lanka also retained the same XI after overcoming Malaysia and Pakistan to reach the gold-medal match. India's semifinal win was powered by Shafali's unbeaten 100 off 49 balls.The final is a rematch of the 2023 Asian Games gold-medal clash, as well as the Women's Asia Cup final earlier this month, both won by India. India are defending their Asian Games title after winning gold in their only previous appearance in the women's cricket event in 2023.Sri Lanka, meanwhile, are seeking their first Asian Games gold after winning bronze in 2014 and silver in 2022. Mandhana's 11,000-run milestone has added another historic subplot to the gold-medal showdown.
Article Summary: Smriti Mandhana becomes first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs in international cricket during India's Asian Games gold-medal final against Sri Lanka. The 30-year-old entered the final needing just 13 runs to reach the landmark. The milestone added another chapter to a remarkable run of record- breaking performances for the left-hander.

Article Title: Smriti Mandhana, Richa Ghosh power India to highest-ever Asian Games total in gold-medal match vs Sri Lanka
Article Text:
Team India (Pic credit: BCCI Women)

SCORECARD:

Mandhana lays foundation before Richa's late assault

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana 's blistering 79 and Richa Ghosh's explosive unbeaten 49 helped India post a daunting 216/3, their highest-ever total in women's cricket at the Asian Games, against Sri Lanka in the gold-medal match at the Korogi Sports Park on Tuesday.Batting first after Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss, India came out attacking from the outset, with Mandhana setting the tone in the opening over. The left-hander struck two boundaries off Sugandika Kumari before continuing her assault in the third over, smashing two successive sixes off the Sri Lankan bowler.Shafali Verma soon joined the party, and India raced to 40/0 after four overs. The fifth over, bowled by Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu, yielded 19 runs, including three sixes, as the opening pair took India to 59/0. India finished the powerplay at 67/0.Mandhana reached her 37th T20I half-century from 31 balls in the 10th over. The milestone was even more significant as she also became the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs in international cricket.However, India lost Shafali later in the same over. Chamudi Praboda dismissed the opener for a brisk 48 off 29 balls, ending India's 99-run opening partnership.Shafali's innings featured three fours and three sixes.Mandhana continued to anchor India's innings as Harmanpreet joined her in the middle. The pair took India to 123/1 after 13 overs before Kavisha Dilhari ended their 42-run partnership by dismissing Harmanpreet for 19 off 17 balls.Richa then joined Mandhana and immediately maintained the tempo. The pair added 15 runs from Praboda's 16th over, taking India to 157/2.Sri Lanka finally got the prized wicket of Mandhana in the 17th over when Sugandika Kumari dismissed her for 79 off 45 balls. Mandhana's innings included five fours and seven sixes, leaving India at 163/3.There was no let-up in India's scoring after her departure. Richa took charge, smashing 14 runs from Kavya Kavindi's over as India crossed 180.The wicketkeeper-batter saved her most damaging assault for the final over. Taking on Mithali Ayodhya, Richa smashed 17 runs to propel India to 216/3 after 20 overs.Richa remained unbeaten on 49 off just 22 balls, with six fours and three sixes, narrowly missing a half-century but ensuring India finished with a formidable total.For Sri Lanka, Praboda, Dilhari and Kumari claimed one wicket apiece.The 216/3 surpassed India's previous best total in women's cricket at the Asian Games and gave the defending champions a substantial platform as they looked to retain the gold medal.
Article Summary: Smriti Mandhana's 79 and Richa Ghosh's unbeaten 49 help India post 216/3. It is India's highest-ever total in women's cricket at the Asian Games. India beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the gold-medal match.

Article Title: NBA contract update: Toronto Raptors signs 23-year-old 6-foot-3er guard to multi-year deal for $9.4 million
Article Text:
Jaden Bradley gets four-year commitment from Raptors. Image via: Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images

Jaden Bradley lands four-year Raptors deal

Bradley now fights for backup point guard minutes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jaden Bradley just turned a training camp battle into a four-year paycheck. The Toronto Raptors converted the 23-year-old guard's two-way contract into a standard deal worth $9.3 million on Monday, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, with the first season fully guaranteed.Toronto's roster had dropped to 13 players once the long-negotiated Kawhi Leonard trade finally cleared, sending Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick out west. Someone had to fill that open standard spot, and Bradley made the case himself.Jaden Bradley arrived in Toronto as the 50th pick of the 2026 draft, a slot usually reserved for camp fodder, not four-year commitments. He signed a two-way deal back on July 6 and spent the summer trying to make himself impossible to cut loose.He didn't dominate Summer League so much as show some unforgettable moments. Across five games, the Rochester, New York native averaged 6.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists in just over 20 minutes a night, topping out at 15 points and five boards in a July 13 win over Indiana. Scotto's report on the new deal noted that "this first year of the deal is guaranteed," a detail that matters for a player who came in as one of the draft's final names.Bradley spent his final three college seasons at Arizona after starting his career at Alabama, where he made the All-SEC freshman team. By his senior year with the Wildcats, he was Big 12 Player of the Year, averaging 13.3 points, 4.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals while shooting 39.4 percent from three. He picked up Big 12 Tournament MVP and consensus Third Team All-American honors along the way and helped drag Arizona to its first Final Four in 25 years.None of that guarantees playing time in Toronto. Bradley will spend training camp, which opens September 29 in Quebec City, competing for backup point guard reps behind Immanuel Quickley, with fellow Big 12 products Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter already in that mix. It's a crowded lane for a player who was a fringe draft name three months ago.Toronto didn't leave its two-way roster thin in the process. The team filled Bradley's old two-way slot with former Gonzaga guard Malachi Smith, keeping that development pipeline active even as Bradley graduates to the standard roster.For now, the deal looks like an investment rather than a promise for playing minutes. The Raptors are betting that the ball-handling, defense, and playmaking instincts that carried Arizona to a Final Four run translate better once an NBA season actually starts. Bradley gets four years and a guaranteed first season to prove it.
Article Summary: Jaden Bradley signed a two-way contract with the Toronto Raptors back on July 6. The 23-year-old guard now has a four-year deal with the Raptors worth $9.3 million. Bradley will compete for backup point guard minutes in training camp.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark’s $20M fortune gets attention, but her $100,000+ cereal campaign reveals a different side of her WNBA success and community work
