Caitlin Clark’s $20M fortune gets attention, but her $100,000+ cereal campaign reveals a different side of her WNBA success and community work (Image via Getty: Caitlin Clark)

How did Caitlin Clark’s cereal campaign raise more than $100,000 for youth programmes?

Caitlin Clark’s $20M fortune is only one part of her story away from basketball

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark’s rise in women’s basketball has brought plenty of attention to her growing profile off the court. One of the more unusual examples came through a box of cereal, as her Caitlin’s Crunch Time partnership with Hy-Vee turned a popular food product into a fundraising effort for young people.The campaign raised more than $100,000 for the Caitlin Clark Foundation, with the money supporting programmes centred on education, nutrition and sports across the Midwest. It offered fans a simple way to connect with Clark’s community work while supporting causes linked closely to her foundation.Per Caitlin Clark foundation website, the idea began as a partnership between Clark, her foundation and Hy-Vee. Caitlin’s Crunch Time cereal returned to Hy-Vee stores across the Midwest in May 2025 after an earlier limited release in Iowa. Hy-Vee pledged a percentage of the proceeds from each box sold to the Caitlin Clark Foundation.The partnership had a personal connection to Clark’s own story. Her foundation focuses on three areas: education, nutrition and sports, which it describes as pillars that played an important role in her development as an athlete. The cereal campaign gave fans a simple way to support that work while buying a product connected to Clark.“Having my own cereal is a fun way to connect with fans,” Clark said when Hy-Vee announced the 2025 release. She also thanked the company for supporting the foundation and its mission to improve the lives of young people.By Jan. 2026, the foundation announced that the campaign had raised more than $100,000. It said the funds would help support local initiatives across the Midwest, giving the campaign a purpose beyond the product itself.The partnership also forms part of a longer relationship between Clark and Hy-Vee. The foundation said the company had raised approximately $500,000 for its work through its partnership with Clark.Clark’s commercial rise has been rapid since she became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball. Celebrity Net Worth currently estimates her net worth at $20 million and lists her 2026 WNBA salary at roughly $530,000. The site also reports that she earned about $16 million from endorsements in 2025 and has an estimated $28 million Nike deal running over eight years.Those figures show the scale of Clark’s success away from the basketball court, but the cereal campaign offers a different look at how that commercial profile can be connected to her foundation’s work.The campaign was not simply a personal $100,000 donation from Clark. The more than $100,000 figure represents money raised through Caitlin's Crunch Time campaign, while Hy-Vee provided the retail platform and pledged proceeds to the foundation.That distinction is important because Clark’s community work often involves partnerships that turn her popularity into support for youth programmes. Her foundation says its goal is to create opportunities for children to learn, grow and thrive through education, nutrition and sports.In Clarks’ case, the cereal became more than a piece of merchandise. It connected her growing commercial profile with a cause that sits at the centre of her foundation’s work, while giving fans another way to participate in that effort.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark’s Crunch Time partnership with Hy-Vee turned a popular food product into a fundraising effort for young people. The campaign raised more than $100,000 for the Caitlin Clark Foundation, with the money supporting programmes centred on education, nutrition and sports. Celebrity Net Worth currently estimates her net worth at $20 million.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 6: How Nihal Sarin blundered his queen, and India suffered heartbreaking loss to Uzbekistan
Article Text:
Nihal Sarin at Chess Olympiad (Photo by Michal Walusza from FIDE)

India's women back to winning ways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: On Monday, India's open team was paired against hot favourites and tournament hosts Uzbekistan in Round 6 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.The anticipation around this fixture had been building since before the tournament began, perhaps because these two nations have won the last two Olympiads between them, or because Dommaraju Gukesh will face Javokhir Sindarov for the World Championship later this year, or simply because these are, right now, two of the most potent chess nations on the planet.India had arrived at the board sitting in the leading group after five rounds, level with Uzbekistan and Germany at the top of the standings, which only added to the stakes. Hence, captain Srinath Narayanan put the strongest line-up forward, with Praggnanandhaa on Board 1, Arjun Erigaisi on 2, Nihal Sarin on 3, and Gukesh on 4.Consequently, Vidit Gujrathi had a rest day, thanks to which he was momentarily part of the ChessBase India commentary team at the venue.His eyes lit up when Nodirbek Yakubboev, playing White, pushed 35.f4 against Nihal. With every other board on the day ending in or heading towards a draw, this was the one game left with a winner in it.Nihal replied 35...e3, and Vidit's eyes only became brighter. Yakubboev's 36.fxg5+ put India in a genuinely promising position.But then what followed was a sequence no Indian fan would have wanted to see — 36...Kxg5 37.g3 Nf5.Vidit felt Nihal, sensing a clear advantage, got swept up in the moment and pushed a little too hard. Soon after, his queen was captured (40.Qxc7), and the entire commentary panel, Vidit included, could only put their hands on their heads.The disappointment was more palpable because Nihal still had plenty of time left on the clock. This wasn't a case of time pressure forcing a mistake, just a hanging piece missed in the heat of a winning position. But that is what it was.Amid all that activity, Nihal's queen was left completely undefended on c7. Yakubboev's 40.Qxc7 simply took it for free.From a position where Black had real winning chances just a few moves earlier, the game swung entirely in White's favour, and Yakubboev converted the resulting material advantage into a full point without much further resistance.It proved decisive. With Praggnanandhaa, Erigaisi and Gukesh all drawing their games on the other three boards, Nihal's loss was the difference. Uzbekistan won the match 2.5-1.5, handing India their first team defeat of the tournament in the open section.India's women, by contrast, had a comfortable day at the office after a Round 5 defeat to Poland, beating the United States 3-1 on Monday.Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh both drew their games against higher-pedigree opposition in Carissa Yip and Alice Lee, but the difference came further down the order, with Vantika Agrawal beating the experienced Irina Krush, and Savitha Shri getting the better of Rose Atwell.Tuesday is the tournament's only scheduled rest day, a timely break for India's open side after a result that will sting more for how close it came to going the other way than for the actual damage on the scoreboard.Play resumes on Wednesday with Round 7, when India's open team takes on England, and the women's team faces Germany.
Article Summary: India's open team was paired against hot favourites and tournament hosts Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan won the match 2.5-1.5, handing India their first team defeat of the tournament in the open section. India's women, by contrast, had a comfortable day at the office after a Round 5 defeat to Poland, beating the United States 3-1 on Monday.

Article Title: ‘Virat Kohli inspires me’: Himanshu Dhillon’s dream Asian Games debut with two silvers
Article Text:
India's Rudrankksh Patil, left, wins bronze medal and Himanshu Dhillon wins Silver medal (PTI Photo)

From wrestling to shooting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Himanshu Dhillon is a diehard Sunny Deol fan. His father, Shamsher Dhillon, has a doctorate in agriculture. The shooter’s motivational mantra, then, paraphrases a famous dialogue of his idol, his father’s profession and the farming he tried during the pandemic.“Yeh kisaan ka haath hai. Yeh lohe ko pighla kar uska aakaar badal deta hai (This is the hand of a farmer. He melts iron and shapes it).”On Monday, Dhillon didn’t melt metal; instead, he shot two of them, both silver, in the 10m air rifle at the Aichi Prefecture Shooting Range.First, the Asian Games debutant teamed up with Rudrankksh Patil and Parth Mane to clinch the men’s team silver. He returned later in the afternoon and, in a pulsating display of composure, concentration and precision, finished second (252.4) in the individual event, opening his individual tally at the senior international level.Patil, who at one stage held a 1.5-point lead, faltered and settled for bronze (230.9).It took a Games record by the reigning Olympic and Asian Games champion Lihao Sheng (254.2) to climb to the top of the podium. The Chinese shooter bettered his mark of 253.3 from the previous Games.Dhillon’s father sends him motivational messages daily. On the day, first came his 21st birthday wishes, followed by a message which read: “Whatever happens, you need to add a medal for India.The colour of the medal depends on you.”The message, in his native tongue, seemed to strike a chord. While Patil hit the front, Sheng and Dhillon played catch-up. A 10.2 and 9.7 relegated Patil. Dhillon was also pegged back by a 9.8, which gave the Chinese the unassailable lead, but his three 10.9s did the trick.It was a contest of fine margins, with four 10.9s in an elimination series and three shoot-offs deciding positions.Dhillon’s journey is only beginning, but the junior World Cup gold medallist already has an eye on the legacy he would like. In shooting, he idolises Abhinav Bindra . His sporting hero, though, is Virat Kohli “I’m very inspired by Virat Kohli,” he said.As he walked away with two silver medals around his neck, the significance of the day was not lost on him.“This is the best birthday gift I could have given myself,” he said.But he did not begin as a shooter. Inspired by his uncle Hardeep Singh Dhillon, who represented India in Greco-Roman wrestling at the 2016 Rio Olympics, his father enrolled him in an akhada. It took just two weeks to realise wrestling was not for him.“I found wrestling a bit hard, so I later opted for shooting while studying in a Gurukul in Kudri,” he said with a laugh.Once he found his calling at the range, his family backed him despite financial constraints.“My parents left our village for me. It’s their sacrifices that have got me here,” he said.
Article Summary: Himanshu Dhillon won two silver medals at the Asian Games. He teamed up with Rudrankksh Patil and Parth Mane to clinch the men’s team silver. He returned later in the afternoon and finished second (252.4) in the individual event.

Article Title: In 2013, Pink paid nearly $9 million for a 200-acre California ranch with a 10,000-sq-ft home; 13 years later, the estate has become a working organic vineyard producing her Two Wolves wine
Article Text:
Pink said she had never had a female mentor before working on Two Wolves. (Photo: Forbes)

Learning to make wine

Why organic farming became central

Building Two Wolves

Singer Alecia Beth Moore-Hart, known professionally as Pink, bought a 200-acre ranch in California’s Santa Barbara County with her husband Carey Hart in 2013 for almost $9 million. The property included a vineyard. Thirteen years later, the land is also home to Two Wolves Wine, the label she created after spending years learning about winemaking and organic farming.The purchase came while wine was still a growing interest for Pink, Forbes reported. She found the property online while she was on tour in Australia and bought it without seeing it herself. She sent Hart to look at it before the purchase. The couple had already been visiting the Santa Ynez area for about 20 years, riding motorcycles and stopping at wineries along the way. According to Realtor, apart from the vineyard, the property included a 10-bedroom, 10,000-square-foot estate, a pool and a spa.Pink's interest in wine had started much earlier. She told Forbes that she did not grow up drinking wine and once thought it was 'punishment at holiday dinners'.That changed in her 20s, when people in her management team introduced her to better wines and wineries while she was on tour. She began visiting vineyards during breaks from performances and later studied about it through Wine and Spirit Educational Trust courses and UCLA Extension.Pink eventually began learning about the work that goes into producing it, including farming grapes and caring for the land. While touring for her concerts, she continued her studies backstage. She would finish performances and then open her laptop to study wine. Her interest in wineries also took her to places such as Penfolds and Clos Rougeard, where she learned from winemakers and asked questions about their methods.After buying the California property, Pink began making wine herself. She initially worked on small batches in a refrigerated garage, starting with a single macro bin. She was not planning to release the wine commercially at first. Instead, she was making it because she wanted to learn.Winemaker Alison Thomson later became her partner and co-winemaker. The two met at a dinner party, which Pink described as a kind of 'stealth dinner party interview'. Thomson did not know she was being considered for the role at the time. She eventually joined Pink in developing the wines.Pink's first vintage was made in 2014. She kept the project largely private for several years before deciding to release the wine. The first Two Wolves bottling finally came out in 2018.At the time, Pink said she was concerned that people in the wine industry might not take her seriously because she was a celebrity. "I was worried that people would think I was a clown." She said she did not want to simply put her name on a bottle made by someone else. "I really rolled up my sleeves," she said.Organic farming is a major part of the Two Wolves project. The vineyard Pink bought was certified organic, and she has continued to make that approach central to the operation.Pink explained her concern about the use of pesticides by pointing to the possible risks for vineyard workers. "You hear horror stories of a vineyard worker that got cut with pesticides in his leg, and now he's an amputee. Real stories," she said.Thomson, who studied restorative ecology before working in wine, also described the vineyard as a complete system. The team uses cover crops, which are plants grown to help support soil and the wider vineyard environment. It also has native plantings, owl boxes and bluebird boxes.Thomson said the aim is to maintain healthy soil with good drainage and nutrients. These factors matter because grapevines depend on the soil in which they grow, while the plants and animals around them form part of the wider vineyard ecosystem.The wines are grown on 25 certified-organic acres in Santa Barbara County. This is part of the larger 200-acre ranch that Pink and Hart bought in 2013.The winery's name comes from a teaching story about two wolves living inside a person. One represents qualities such as greed, envy, anger, jealousy, selfishness and fear, while the other represents curiosity, compassion, generosity and love. When asked which wolf wins, the answer is, "The one you feed."Pink said she has always known the story as a Cherokee legend, while noting that the Two Wolves property sits on Chumash land. For her, the story represents balance and the choices people make.The winery has also become a project led by women. Pink built the Two Wolves team with five women. Thomson said the project gave her an opportunity to continue working in wine while also having space for family life.Pink said she had never had a female mentor before working on Two Wolves. She described the experience of working with women in charge as different from what she had known earlier in her career.
Article Summary: Singer Alecia Beth Moore-Hart, known professionally as Pink, bought a 200-acre ranch in California’s Santa Barbara County with her husband Carey Hart in 2013 for almost $9 million. Thirteen years later, the land is also home to Two Wolves Wine, the label she created after spending years learning about winemaking and organic farming. Pink said she had never had a female mentor before working on Two Wolves.

Article Title: 7pm Kalkaji Mandir visit, 7.30pm park, 8.45pm PCR call: Timeline of how 3 fake cops gang-raped Delhi teen
Article Text:
A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men in Astha Kunj Park. T

7pm: Darshan at Kalkaji Mandir

7.30pm: Three men allegedly pose as cops

8.45pm: PCR call triggers police action

Police launch hunt for accused





NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir after the accused allegedly posed as policemen and separated her from her male friend, Delhi Police said.The incident unfolded over a little more than an hour on Sunday, according to the police account.The girl and her male friend had gone to Kalkaji Mandir for darshan at around 7pm, police said. After visiting the temple, the two entered the nearby Astha Kunj Park through Gate No. 7.While the two were inside the park, three men allegedly approached them and claimed to be policemen. The men allegedly separated the girl from her friend and took her towards a secluded area.One of the accused, identified as Asif, allegedly threatened the girl with a firearm and a knife before sexually assaulting her. The other two men also allegedly sexually assaulted her, police said.The three accused subsequently allegedly threatened the girl and her friend.A PCR call regarding the alleged rape was received at around 8.45pm. The SHO of Amar Colony police station and police staff reached Astha Kunj Park, where they found the girl and her friend.The girl was subsequently medically examined at AIIMS. Crime and forensic teams examined the spot and collected relevant exhibits.Based on her statement, an FIR was registered at Amar Colony police station under sections 70(2), 61(2), 115(2) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 6 and 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.Several police teams were formed to trace the three accused during the investigation.A team led by Inspector Rajender Dagar, in-charge of the Special Staff of South-East district, received information about Asif's movement near DM Office Road in Amar Colony and laid a trap, police said.When the police team intercepted him, Asif allegedly opened fire at the officers. Police said he fired three rounds despite being asked to surrender.One of the rounds hit head constable Rajesh's bulletproof jacket. Police said the constable fired two rounds in self-defence, one of which struck Asif in his right leg.Asif was injured and taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre for treatment. Crime and forensic teams were also called to the encounter spot as the investigation continued.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men in Astha Kunj Park. The accused allegedly posed as policemen and separated her from her male friend. The incident unfolded over a little more than an hour on Sunday, according to police.

Article Title: Delhi trekker found dead in 400m gorge in Uttarakhand’s Chopta while trying to take photograph
Article Text:
A woman from Delhi tragically lost her life during a solo trip to Chopta when she slipped and fell into a deep gorge

Poll Vote & Share your view What's the most important aspect of safety during hiking or trekking? Proper gear Guided tours Weather awareness Emergency services access 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





DEHRADUN: A 26-year-old woman from Delhi’s Shahdara area, who went missing on Sunday afternoon during a solo trip to Uttarakhand’s Chopta, was found dead on Monday in a 400 m-deep gorge below Ravan Shila along the Chopta-Tungnath trekking route.Police suspect she slipped and fell while trying to take a photograph.The victim, Pooja Sahni, had left Delhi on Sept 19, telling her family she was going out to look for a job. Instead, she travelled alone and reached Rudraprayag on the morning of Sept 20.When she did not return home, her family filed a missing person complaint at the Welcome police station in Delhi.Rudraprayag police were alerted on Sunday evening that a person may have fallen from a rocky stretch frequently used by tourists and trekkers for photography, according to sub-inspector Manwar Singh.A State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) team launched an initial search near Tungnath temple on Sunday evening, but operations were suspended due to darkness.The search resumed at 7:10 am on Monday, leading to the recovery of Sahni’s body from the gorge. In coordination with District Disaster Response Force (DDRF) and local police, the SDRF team carried the body on a stretcher across three kilometres of difficult terrain back to Chopta.“It appears that she climbed onto the rock to click a picture, lost her balance and fell into the gorge,” SI Singh said, noting that gusty winds were blowing in the area on Sunday evening.Police in Rudraprayag stated that the victim’s family was expected to arrive in Augustmuni by Monday night.Further details regarding her background and the exact circumstances of the fall are under investigation.
Article Summary: Pooja Sahni, 26, went missing on Sunday afternoon during a solo trip to Uttarakhand’s Chopta. She was found dead on Monday in a 400 m-deep gorge below Ravan Shila along the Chopta-Tungnath trekking route. Police suspect she slipped and fell while trying to take a photograph.

Article Title: Swept away by raging Teesta in Bengal, elephant calf saved by four fishermen
Article Text:
The elephant calf being rescued from the Teesta

Poll Vote & Share your view What was the most remarkable part of the elephant calf rescue story? The fishermen's courage The reunion with its mother The teamwork involved 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





Jalpaiguri: Five Jalpaiguri fishermen on a small row boat pulled off a miraculous rescue on Teesta as they pulled up a newborn elephant calf on Monday. The calf had been swept away nearly 4 km downstream while its herd was crossing the river near Apalchand forest’s Kathambari range.Spotting the calf struggling to stay afloat, Bablu Das, Mithun Das, Kader Das, Biswanath and Gopal braved the swollen river’s strong currents and rowed their boat to the elephant. The calf was gasping for breath, with its little trunk raised above the water as the waves continued to push it further downstream. Three of the fishermen jumped off and the calf was hauled on to the boat. As the boat returned, the three swam alongside the boat, pushing it against the current.The calf was handed over to forest personnel upon reaching the bank. It was taken to the Kathambari range office and given immediate veterinary care.Earlier on Monday, a herd of five elephants was moving upstream of Gajoldoba Teesta Barrage when currents separated the calf. The fishermen spotted it floating near the 12th spur of Teesta, close to Punjab embankment.Following the rescue, teams from Baikunthapur forest division began efforts to locate the mother.The calf was transported across the barrage to a dry stretch of Teesta riverbed, where the herd was believed to have taken shelter.After nearly two hours of coordinated efforts of foresters, locals and fishermen, the calf was successfully reunited with its mother. The mother elephant approached the calf and was later seen nursing it.Baikunthapur DFO Mudit lauded the fishermen for their timely action, saying it was crucial for the reunion. Elephants often don’t take back calves into the herd if they are exposed to humans for long. During the north Bengal floods last Oct, a calf rescued from Mechi river was rejected by its herd.
Article Summary: Five Jalpaiguri fishermen on a small row boat pulled off a miraculous rescue on Teesta as they pulled up a newborn elephant calf. The calf had been swept away nearly 4 km downstream while its herd was crossing the river near Apalchand forest’s Kathambari range.

Article Title: Pune techie kills pregnant wife, cooks up robbery story; jumps from 2nd floor
Article Text:
A software engineer who took the life of his three-month-pregnant wife and attempted to disguise it as a robbery (Representative image generated using AI)





PUNE: A 31-year-old software engineer allegedly killed his three-month-pregnant wife at their rented home in Dehugaon early on Sunday, staged a robbery and jumped from the second floor of the building to mislead investigators, police said on Monday.Akash Baraskar, who is being treated at a hospital, allegedly slit the throat of his wife, Shubhangi (28), and later told investigators that robbers had attacked the couple.Police said the claim fell apart after residents reported that the couple had been quarrelling until 4am.Senior police inspector Vikram Bansode of Dehu Road police said, “Around 6am on Sunday, we received information that a person had been attacked in Dehugaon. On reaching the spot, a police team found Baraskar lying on the ground.”He said, “Baraskar told police that robbers had attacked him and his wife and that she was lying in their second-floor rented accommodation. Police found the woman severely injured and unconscious.”Police took the couple to a hospital, where doctors pronounced Shubhangi dead.“Though we began probing a robbery attempt, we became suspicious when residents of the building told us the couple had been quarrelling until 4am on Sunday.They also told us that the couple had been quarrelling ever since they moved into the building about five months ago,” Bansode said.“During questioning, he admitted to killing his wife with a sharp weapon. He then inflicted injuries on himself and jumped from the balcony,” the officer said.Baraskar is from Ahilyanagar district and works with a software company in Hinjewadi. Shubhangi worked for a private company. They got married in 2023.Shubhangi’s father, in his complaint lodged on Sunday night, alleged that Baraskar had been harassing his daughter because she opposed his decision to buy farmland in his hometown in Ahilyanagar district.He also accused Baraskar of neglecting her despite knowing that she was pregnant.Baraskar, who is undergoing treatment at a hospital, has been charged under Section 103 (murder) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). He will be taken into custody once he is discharged.

Article Title: Calicut FC footballer Rijohn Jose killed in accident in Kozhikode
Article Text:
Rijohn, who played as a defender, was a native of Ollur in Thrissur.





KOZHIKODE: Calicut Football Club player Rijohn Jose, 29, died in a bike accident in Kozhikode late on Sunday night. His teammate Gani Ahmed Nigam, 28, who was pillion riding, sustained a leg injury.The accident occurred around 10.40pm on the Gandhi Road flyover near Christian College.The two players were returning to their accommodation near the beach after dinner when a motorcycle coming from the opposite direction lost control and collided with their bike.The impact threw both players onto the road. Rijo, who was riding the bike, suffered serious injuries to his head and chest.Those who took the injured players to hospital said it was raining at the time of the accident and that passing vehicles did not stop despite their attempts to seek help. After a while, an ambulance arrived and took them to a private hospital in the city. Rijohn died around 12.15am on Monday.Rijohn, who played as a defender, was a native of Ollur in Thrissur. Hospital authorities said Gani Ahmed Nigam’s condition was stable. Gani has represented Kerala in Santosh Trophy The rider of the other motorcycle, Shahil Rahman of Iringadanpally, sustained serious injuries and is undergoing treatment at Kozhikode medical college hospital (MCH).Calicut FC had announced its squad only recently, and the team was preparing for the Super League Kerala matches scheduled to begin this week. Rijohn and Gani had joined the team just two days ago.Nadakkavu SI N Leela conducted the inquest. After the postmortem at Kozhikode MCH, Rijohn’s body was handed over to his relatives. It was later kept for public viewing at Corporation Stadium before being taken to Ollur in Thrissur.Rijohn was the son of M P Jose of Maliekkal Mukkattukara House, Ollur, and Treesa Jose. The funeral will be held at 11am on Monday at St Raphael’s Church, Ollur.
Article Summary: Calicut Football Club player Rijohn Jose, 29, died in a bike accident in Kozhikode. His teammate Gani Ahmed Nigam, 28, who was pillion riding, sustained a leg injury. The two players were returning to their accommodation near the beach after dinner when a motorcycle lost control and collided with their bike.

Article Text:
A Delhi High Court case explores returning an adopted orphan child years later





NEW DELHI: Can an orphan adopted legally after following all procedures be "returned" years later if the adoptive parents are unable to handle the truant minor or if the child poses a threat to them?The case of one such child, adopted in 2018 by a couple but now proving a handful for the mother, has reached the Delhi high court, which sought the stand of the authorities, reports Abhinav Garg.Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma, during a hearing last week, pointed out that there aren't too many precedents, if any, to shed light on law governing return of a minor in such cases and asked Centre, through Central Adoption Resource Authority, to furnish its stand. HC also issued notice to Child Welfare Committee - Kasturba Niketan Complex at Lajpat Nagar and asked it to respond if the minor can be housed at the facility.Recognising the urgency and importance of the matter, HC asked the authorities to respond by Sept 30. It was hearing a plea filed by the mother of the boy seeking directions to hand over his custody to CARA or any govt organisation or any private organisation, which can also provide all necessary medical care and treatment to the child for which she will bear the expenses to the best of her financial capacity.Explaining her predicament, the woman, through advocate Ali Bin Saif, informed the court that she and her husband adopted the child, then six years old, via CARA in 2018.“It was later discovered that he was intellectually disabled and was indulging in inappropriate behaviour, including aggression, committing theft and was expelled from multiple schools,” Saif submitted, adding that three years after the adoption, the woman lost her husband and is now living with her mother and sister.“The petitioner and her husband adopted the respondent no. 4 (boy) at the age of 6 years and either his medical examination was not conducted in the proper manner or the concerned doctors were not able to detect his illness,” the plea says, adding that the couple admitted him in a school where he behaved inappropriately with a schoolmate. “The petitioner was informed about such incident by the school authority and the boy was expelled from the school. ”Highlighting that three aged women are at present grappling with the boy, the petition says that due to his behaviour, petitioner and her old age mother are in constant fear that he will misbehave. The petition adds that he has been expelled from many schools and “due to mental disability, the petitioner is in constant fear that the boy can do anything with her if she stopped him from stealing money or misbehaving”.Seeking the court’s intervention, the mother says that with passage of time the adopted son is “becoming more violent and there is apprehension that he can misbehave... and therefore it is not safe for the petitioner and her mother and her sister.”
Article Summary: Delhi High Court case explores returning an adopted orphan child years later. Can an orphan adopted legally be "returned" years later if the adoptive parents are unable to handle the truant minor or if the child poses a threat to them? The case of one such child, adopted in 2018 by a couple but now proving a handful for the mother.

Article Title: Malviya Nagar fire: HC grants bail to hotel owner on medical grounds
Article Text: New Delhi: Delhi High Court Monday granted four weeks’ interim bail to the owner of a Malviya Nagar hotel where a fire claimed 23 lives in June.Justice Sachin Datta granted the relief to Lovkesh Bajaj on medical grounds, noting that he underwent a major abdominal surgery on Aug 31 and was discharged from the hospital only on Sept 15.“From the aforesaid (medical) report, it is also evident that there is a risk of complications, warranting careful medical management,” the court noted.It added that “having regard to the nature of the surgery undergone by the applicant and the short period that has elapsed since his discharge from the hospital, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the present case, the court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be released on interim bail on medical grounds, for a limited period, to enable him to recuperate and recover adequately.”HC directed Bajaj to furnish a personal bond of Rs 25,000 and a surety of the like amount and remain within the territory of Delhi.Presently in judicial custody, Bajaj has been named as an accused in the fire incident at the five-storey ‘Flourish Stay’ B&B in Hauz Rani on June 3, in which 23 people died, and 24 others were injured.On Sept 3, a trial court rejected his plea seeking interim bail of four weeks on medical grounds, saying he was already receiving adequate specialised medical treatment in custody and that the medical exigency cited by the accused had already been addressed through surgery at RML Hospital.According to the investigation, Bajaj had applied for a hotel licence, but it was rejected as the property had only one entry and exit point and lacked a fire exit.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court grants four weeks' interim bail to hotel owner Lovkesh Bajaj. Court noted that he underwent a major abdominal surgery on Aug 31 and was discharged from the hospital only on Sept 15. 23 people died in the fire incident at the five-storey ‘Flourish Stay’ B&B in Hauz Rani on June 3.

Article Title: Narrow alleys host Ganesh mandals with a large heart
Article Text:
Ganesh Mandircha Raja, Vikhroli, Hukmill Lane Ganpati





MUMBAI: Nondescript lanes in Parel, Matunga and Dharavi contain charming idols self-funded by enterprising working class youth.Swapnakshay, AndheriPresident Devendra Amberkar says their Model Town mandal near Four Bungalows has installed a 9.5-ft paper pulp Ganesh by Vishal Ranjankar. Art director Sumit Patil and lighting designer Shital Talpade have made 'Verses of the Forest' showing a truck loaded with timber bearing bird nests. Birds and animals are pursuing the truck in a desperate attempt to save their homes. A tree is upon an ICU bed in hospital receiving water and fertiliser as saline drip. A four-minute video for devotees highlights environmental protection.Hukmil Lane, Lower ParelOne of the oldest in Lower Parel, this 1934 mandal was started by mill workers from Podar Mill and Apollo Mill, says spokesman Aditya Bachankar. In 1992, Hukmil Lane carved an 18-ft idol from bananas, followed by musical instruments, puja material and coconuts. This year moortikar Arun Datte's unique balancing Ganesh is drawing large crowds to the lane.Labour Camp Cha Sukhkarta, MatungaMandal president Suraj Lot says this is the first time that a 32 ft tall Ganesh moorti has arrived in Matunga Labour Camp. It is also the first time that a hydraulic 'prabhaval' (backdrop) is being used.The enterprising locality has several charming Ganpatis. Among them is the Sukhkarta which is cast in the form of Ram Avtar. Elements of the Ramayan highlight this theme, including its writer sage Valmiki and Hanuman who is a main character in the text. Moortikar Aniket Shewale has crafted the idol.Dharavi SharksIn 2003, 13-year-old Neelesh, later called Nilu Anna, installed a 1.5-ft Ganpati idol, marking the genesis of Om Sai Mitra Mandal or Dharavi Sharks. Organiser Martin Nadar says 40 families self-fund the celebration at Damber Compound behind Royal City School. The 5.5 ft Bappa crafted by moortikar Vinayak from Pratiksha Nagar has to pass through a narrow 3.5 ft lane. The Sharks hold their breath, carefully coordinate every movement, and heave a sigh of relief as the idol navigates its way successfully.Ganesh Mandircha Raja, VikhroliLong lines are unfolding near Kabutarkhana in Tagore Nagar 1 as devotees seek glimpse of the Ganesh Mandircha Raja. "Our moorti has been designed in Mahadev avatar in our 13th year," says mandal head Sanket Kate. Co-organiser Raj Nikam says they distribute food to 2,500 people. Moortikar Mitesh Pevekar carved the idol while Harishchandra Gad designed the theme. The decoration is by mandal members themselves.
Article Summary: Nondescript lanes in Parel, Matunga and Dharavi contain charming idols. Ganesh Mandircha Raja, Vikhroli, Hukmill Lane Ganpati and Sukhkarta are among them.

Article Title: Everything about Ganeshotsav is truly beautiful: Hariharan
Article Text:
Singer Hariharan graced the Sakinakyacha Maharaja Ganeshotsav celebrations, offering prayers and performing the uplifting devotional song Sukhkarta Dukhharta for an eager crowd. He reminisced about his childhood experiences during the festival, recalling his early Ganpati rituals. This year was particularly special as his twin grandchildren celebrated their first Ganeshotsav, creating lasting bonds with the traditions. The celebration featured a stunning 43-foot idol of Ganesh that captivated attendees.

'I BEGIN ALL MY SHOWS WITH THE GANPATI SONG 'VIGHNESHWARA'

‘EVERY PUJA IN OUR HOME BEGAN WITH GANPATI PUJA’

‘ARIA WAS SO UPSET AFTER THE VISARJAN’

About Sakinakacha Maharaja





National Award-winning singer Hariharan joined the Ganeshotsav celebrations at Sakinakacha Maharaja as part of the Bombay Times Blockbuster series. The singer visited the pandal to seek Bappa’s blessings and participate in the aarti. To the delight of the devotees gathered there, Hariharan also took to the mic and sang the much-loved devotional song Sukhkarta Dukhharta.Speaking about his visit, Hariharan said, “It was so beautiful to be here with Sakinakacha Ganpati and get photographed with Him. I came to know that they hold a record of being the tallest Ganpati at 43 feet, that’s around four floors!” For Hariharan, the festival also brought back memories of his childhood and his association with Bappa. “We bring home Bappa for three days and this year was extremely special because I was playing my own recently released aarti, and were all singing together. There is another Ganpati song ‘Vighneshwara’ that I love and I begin all my shows with this,” he said.Ganpati has been a part of Hariharan’s life since childhood. Recalling his early memories of the festival, he said, “During my student life I used to pray to Bappa.In our home also, every puja began with a Ganpati puja. I used to stay in Kamla Kunj in Matunga as a child and I remember watching Ganpati processions but since I was a kid, I was not allowed to join.” He also remembers the celebrations in his neighbourhood. “Next to my building was Ganesh Baug and they would have a big Ganpati and had skits, dramas, would show movies, give a different prasad every day. Those are wonderful memories of this special festival.”His connection with Bappa continued into his college years. “Next to Matunga station there used to be a tiny Ganesh Temple. As a collegiate, I’d take a train from Matunga station to VT and walk across the maidan to Government Law College. So every single morning I'd first say a hello to Ganpati Bappa.”This year, Ganeshotsav became particularly special for Hariharan as his twin grandchildren, one-and-a-half-year-old, experienced the festival for the first time. The little ones, he says, quickly formed an attachment to Bappa. “This year my twin grandkids, Aria and Ahaan experienced their first Ganpati and within just these three days they got very attached to Bappa. Aarya was so upset after the visarjan, ‘Where is Bappa, what did you do with him?’ So we had to tell her that Ganpati has gone home for a swim,” he said.For the singer, moments like these capture the enduring beauty of the festival. “This whole concept of Ganeshotsav is absolutely beautiful,” he said.Established in 1985, Sakinakyacha Maharaja Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal has become one of Mumbai’s prominent Ganeshotsav attractions and is known for its towering Ganpati idol. This year, the over 40 feet idol was created on-site over several weeks and has received recognition as 'Mumbai’s tallest Ganesh idol'. It has a regal Peshwai-inspired look, complete with a traditional pheta, sword and trishul.
Article Summary: Singer Hariharan graced the Sakinakyacha Maharaja Ganeshotsav celebrations, offering prayers and performing the uplifting devotional song Sukhkarta Dukhharta for an eager crowd. He reminisced about his childhood experiences during the festival, recalling his early Ganpati rituals. The celebration featured a stunning 43-foot idol of Ganesh that captivated attendees.

Article Title: Burglars hit Nanded cop’s home, flee with service pistol, 30 bullets, gold & cash
Article Text:
Thieves steal cop’s service pistol, 30 live rounds, cash and gold





Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: Burglars broke into a police head constable’s home in Nanded ’s Kautha area and escaped with his service pistol, 30 live cartridges, cash and gold worth a total of Rs 16.7 lakh. Police suspect an interstate gang and have deployed six teams to track down three suspects.The burglary took place at Ram Bagh Residency on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday. The house was empty at the time.Nanded SP Neelabh Rohan said, “Preliminary probe has revealed involvement of three suspects. Six teams have been deployed to work on this and nab the suspects.”Head constable Gajanan Baliram Kadam, posted as a crime writer at Nanded city sub-divisional police officer’s office, discovered the burglary when he returned home around 10 am on Saturday.His family had left for their village Gortha on Sept 17 for the Mahalakshmi festival. Kadam returned home on Sept 18 after work and kept his govt-issued pistol and ammunition inside. With his family away, he stepped out for dinner and later returned to his Wazirabad office for work. He worked late and slept at the office, leaving his home vacant.Police suspect the burglars broke open the lock of the second-floor flat during the night.They allegedly ransacked the house and fled with the pistol, ammunition and valuables.When Kadam returned in the morning, he found the front door open and the lock broken. Household articles were strewn around.According to his complaint, the burglars stole Rs 6.5 lakh in cash and a gold necklace, chain and two rings weighing about five tolas and valued at around Rs 5 lakh. The service pistol and 30 cartridges were also missing. The total stolen property has been valued at Rs 16.7 lakh.Senior police officers inspected the spot. An FIR was registered with Nanded Rural police late Saturday after a panchanama.Inspector Omkant Chincholkar, SDPO Prashant Shinde and local crime branch inspector Atul Bhosle visited the scene. Teams from Nanded Rural police and the local crime branch are trying to trace the suspects and recover the stolen weapon and ammunition.Sub-inspector Dnyaneshwar Bhosle is investigating the case.
Article Summary: Head constable Gajanan Baliram Kadam discovered the burglary when he returned home around 10 am on Saturday. The burglars stole Rs 6.5 lakh in cash and a gold necklace, chain and two rings weighing about five tolas and valued at around Rs 5 lakh. The service pistol and 30 cartridges were also missing.

Article Title: 32 years after he walked away, Kolhapur man finally comes home to his 90-year-old mother
Article Text:
Housabai and hos son Khandu who returned after 32 years

Kolhapur:





Thirty-two years ago, Khandu Shripati Sakate walked away from his home in Rukdi village in Kolhapur district. He was 26. His mother did not know if she would ever see him again. This week, at 58, Khandu finally returned home.Waiting for him was his mother Housabai, now 90 and surviving on a pension of just Rs 2,500 a month. She mostly lives alone in a rented room, occasionally staying with relatives. Khandu’s father, who had worked with a farmers’ cooperative, retired and died years ago without seeing his son return.Around 32 years ago, 26-year-old Khandu ran a cycle repair shop in Rukdi. His family was pressuring him to marry, but he did not want to. According to his paternal aunt, he once banged his head against a wall and injured himself, following which he developed mental health issues.Soon afterwards, Khandu left home. The family did not lodge a missing person complaint.For years, there was no word from him.Then, in 2014, Madurai-based Akshaya Trust found Khandu living as a beggar in Chennai. It moved him to a facility for destitute people. There, he was registered as Pandu Sakthi.His path home opened years later through a chance encounter. A team from Shraddha Foundation in Karjat, founded by Ramon Magsaysay Award winner Bharat Vatwani, had travelled to the Madurai facility to drop off another destitute person. Staff there told the volunteers about a man registered as Pandu Sakthi who spoke Marathi.The volunteers took Khandu to Karjat and began his treatment. Within days, he started remembering his past and told the volunteers he desperately wanted to go home.“He told us that he used to live in Rukadi and talked about his parents, especially father. We carried out search and found his mother Housabai living alone in a rented house. We further enquired among relatives and neighbors and matched the claims,” said Ajay Ransure, a social worker with Shraddha Foundation.“We have reunited him with his mother and relatives. We have given him medicines he will need for two months and will continue to monitor health and provide medicines for next two years,” Ransure said.
Article Summary: Khandu Shripati Sakate walked away from his home in Rukdi village in Kolhapur district when he was 26. His mother Housabai, now 90 and surviving on a pension of just Rs 2,500 a month, lives alone in a rented room. Khandu’s father, who had worked with a farmers’ cooperative, retired and died years ago without seeing his son return.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.
